b.9c57e0b7f0:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Ille nos benedícat, qui sine fine vivit et regnat.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro secúndo Regum
<r>2 Reg 15:1-2</r>
<n>1</n> Igitur post hæc fecit sibi Absalom currus et équites et quinquagínta viros, qui præcéderent eum.
<n>2</n> Et mane consúrgens Absalom stabat iuxta intróitum portæ et omnem virum, qui habébat negótium ut veníret ad regis iudícium, vocábat Absalom ad se et dicébat: De qua civitáte es tu? Qui respóndens aiébat: Ex una tribu Israël ego sum servus tuus.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Audi, Dómine, hymnum et oratiónem, quam servus tuus orat coram te hódie, ut sint óculi tui apérti, et aures tuæ inténtæ,
* Super domum istam die ac nocte.
<r>℣.</r> Réspice, Dómine, de sanctuário tuo, et de excélso cælórum habitáculo.
<r>℟.</r> Super domum istam die ac nocte.
b.fdc718b1f9:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May His blessing be upon us who doth live and reign for ever.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the second book of Samuel
<r>2 Sam 15:1-2</r>
<n>1</n> Now after these things Absalom made himself chariots, and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
<n>2</n> And Absalom rising up early stood by the entrance of the gate, and when any man had business to come to the king's judgment, Absalom called him to him, and said: Of what city art thou? He answered, and said: thy servant is of such a tribe of Israel.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Hearken, O Lord, unto the cry and to the prayer which thy servant prayeth before thee today, that thine eyes may be open and thine ears attend;
* Toward this house day and night.
<r>℣.</r> Look down from thine high and holy place, O Lord, even from heaven thy dwelling.
<r>℟.</r> Toward this house, day and night.
b.6f2c6e7dbd:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Divínum auxílium máneat semper nobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>2 Reg 15:3-5</r>
<n>3</n> Respondebátque ei Absalom: Vidéntur mihi sermónes tui boni et iusti; sed non est qui te áudiat constitútus a rege. Dicebátque Absalom:
<n>4</n> Quis me constítuat iúdicem super terram, ut ad me véniant omnes qui habent negótium et iuste iúdicem?
<n>5</n> Sed et, cum accéderet ad eum homo ut salutáret illum, extendébat manum suam et apprehéndens osculabátur eum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Peccávi super númerum arénæ maris, et multiplicáta sunt peccáta mea: et non sum dignus vidére altitúdinem cæli præ multitúdine iniquitátis meæ: quóniam irritávi iram tuam,
* Et malum coram te feci.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco: et delíctum meum contra me est semper, quia tibi soli peccávi.
<r>℟.</r> Et malum coram te feci.
b.2eef22857c:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> God's most mighty strength alway be His people's staff and stay.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>2 Sam 15:3-5</r>
<n>3</n> And Absalom answered him: thy words seem to me good and just. But there is no man appointed by the king to hear thee. And Absalom said:
<n>4</n> O that they would make me judge over the land, that all that have business might come to me, that I might do them justice.
<n>5</n> Moreover when any man came to him to salute him, he put forth his hand, and took him, and kissed him.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> My sins are many, yea, they are more in number than the sands of the sea; I am not worthy to look up toward heaven because of the multitude of my iniquities; for I have provoked thee to anger;
* And done evil in thy sight.
<r>℣.</r> For I acknowledge my transgression, and my sin is ever before me, for against thee only have I sinned.
<r>℟.</r> And done evil in thy sight.
b.100631158d:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Ad societátem cívium supernórum perdúcat nos Rex Angelórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<r>2 Reg 15:6-8</r>
<n>6</n> Faciebátque hoc omni Israël veniénti ad iudícium ut audirétur a rege, et sollicitábat corda virórum Israël.
<n>7</n> Post quadragínta autem annos, dixit Absalom ad regem David: Vadam et reddam vota mea, quæ vovi Dómino, in Hebron.
<n>8</n> Vovens enim vovit servus tuus, cum esset in Gessur Sýriæ, dicens: Si redúxerit me Dóminus in Ierúsalem, sacrificábo Dómino.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Factum est, dum tólleret Dóminus Elíam per túrbinem in cælum, Eliséus clamábat, dicens:
* Pater mi, pater mi, currus Israël, et auríga eius.
<r>℣.</r> Oro, Dómine, ut fiat spíritus tuus duplex in me. At ille inquit: Si víderis, quando tollar a te, erit tibi quod petísti.
<r>℟.</r> Pater mi, pater mi, currus Israël, et auríga eius.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Pater mi, pater mi, currus Israël, et auríga eius.

<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May He that is the Angels' King to that high realm His people bring.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<r>2 Sam 15:6-8</r>
<n>6</n> And this he did to all Israel that came for judgment, to be heard by the king, and he enticed the hearts of the men of Israel.
<n>7</n> And after forty years, Absalom said to king David: Let me go, and pay my vows which I have vowed to the Lord in Hebron.
<n>8</n> For thy servant made a vow, when he was in Gessur of Syria, saying: If the Lord shall bring me again into Jerusalem I will offer sacrifice to the Lord.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> And it came to pass when the Lord would take up Elijah into heaven by a whirlwind Elisha cried, and said:
* My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof.
<r>℣.</r> Oro, Dómine, ut fiat spíritus tuus duplex in me. At ille inquit: Si víderis, quando tollar a te, erit tibi quod petísti.
<r>℟.</r> My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof.
b.98ecba59bb:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, cuius providéntia in sui dispositióne non fállitur: te súpplices exorámus; ut nóxia cuncta submóveas, et ómnia nobis profutúra concédas.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.aa3035acc4:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Whose never-failing Providence ordereth all things both in heaven and earth, we humbly beseech thee to put away from us all hurtful things, and to give us those things which be profitable for us.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.e0df75a5df:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>O</c>ctávo Idus Iúlii Luna quarta. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>S</h>anctæ Elísabeth Víduæ, Lusitanórum Regínæ, quæ ad regnum cæléste quarto Nonas huius mensis transívit.
<h>I</h>n Asia minóre sanctórum Aquilæ et Priscíllæ uxóris, de quibus in Actibus Apostolórum scríbitur.
<h>H</h>erbípoli, in Germánia, sancti Chiliáni Epíscopi, qui, a Románo Pontífice ad prædicándum Evangélium missus, ibi, cum multos ad Christum perduxísset, una cum sóciis Colománno Presbýtero, et Totnáno Diácono, trucidátus est.
<h>I</h>n Portu Románo sanctórum quinquagínta mílitum Mártyrum, qui, in sanctæ Bonósæ confessióne ad fidem addúcti, et a beáto Felíce Papa Primo baptizáti, in Aureliáni Imperatóris persecutióne occísi sunt.
<h>C</h>æsaréæ, in Palæstína, sancti Procópii Mártyris, qui, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, a Scythópoli ductus Cæsaréam, illic, ad primam responsiónum eius confidéntiam, a Iúdice Fabiáno est cápite cæsus.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli pássio sanctórum Monachórum Abrahamitárum, qui ob cultum sanctárum Imáginum, resisténtes Theóphilo Imperatóri, martýrium consummárunt.
<h>S</h>pinæ Lambérti, in Æmília, sancti Hadriáni Papæ Tértii, stúdio conciliándi Románæ Ecclésias Orientáles insígnis, ac miráculis clari; cuius corpus in monastérium Nonantulénse fuit delátum, et in æde sancti Silvéstri honorífice cónditum.
<h>T</h>réviris sancti Auspícii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>R</h>omæ beáti Eugénii Papæ Tértii, qui, postquam cœnóbium sanctórum Vincéntii et Anastásii ad Aquas Sálvias magna sanctimóniæ ac prudéntiæ laude rexísset, Ecclésiam univérsam, Póntifex Máximus renuntiátus, sanctíssime gubernávit. Cultum autem, ab immemorábili témpore ipsi exhíbitum, Pius Papa Nonus ratum hábuit et confirmávit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.39faa7bf9f:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>uly 8th 2027, the 4th day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the feast of the holy widow Isabel, Queen of Portugal, famous for her graces and miracles, [in the year 1336,] whom Pope Urban VIII enrolled among the Saints.
<h>U</h>pon the same 8th day of July, were born into the better life:
<h>I</h>n Lesser Asia, the holy Aquila and Priscilla his wife, of whom the holy Evangelist Luke writeth in the Acts of the Apostles [xviii, 2]
<h>A</h>t Wurzburg, in Germany, holy Killan, Bishop of that city. [An Irish monk, who travelled to Rome in the year 686, was sent by the Roman Pontiff Conon to preach the Gospel.]
<h>W</h>hen he had turned many to Christ he was murdered, [in the year 689,] along with Colman a Priest and Tatnan a Deacon.
<h>A</h>t Porto, in Italy, fifty holy soldiers, all martyrs, who were brought to the faith through the testifying of holy Bonosa, baptized by the blessed Pope Felix, and slain in the persecution under the Emperor Aurelian.
<h>I</h>n Palestine, the holy martyr Procopius. In the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian he was brought from Bethshan, [where he Was reader, exorcist, and interpreter in the church,] to Caesarea, where at the constancy of his very first answers he was beheaded by the command of Fabian the judge.
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, the holy Abrahamite monks, who resisted the Emperor Theophilus concerning the worship of the holy images, and therefore suffered martyrdom.
<h>A</h>t Trier, the holy Confessor Auspicius, Bishop [of that see, fifth century.]
<h>A</h>t Rome, the blessed Pope Eugenius III. He had been Abbot of the monastery of SS. Vincent and Anastatius, near Rome, before he was made Supreme Pontiff. He ruled the universal Church with wonderful holiness and wisdom. [His name was Bernard Paganelli, and he was a native of Pisa, and Canon of that city. He then became a monk of Cîteaux and disciple of St. Bernard before being elected Pope on February 15, 1145, and consecrated in the Benedictine Abbey of Farfa on the 16th of that month. He died at Tivoli on July 8, 1153.]
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
